notes: Identity assessment: the canonical text is a completed primary data-analytic replication report by Esteban Méndez Chacón, titled Data-analytic replication attempt to evaluate 5 claims from Raley_JournMarFam_2012_D2LY, SCORE RR ID 65o96, OSF project qgm2c. Its references identify Raley, Kim and Daniels (2012), the matching original title and DOI 10.1111/j.1741-3737.2012.00990.x. Results, sample sizes, five claim evaluations, materials and references occupy printed pages 1–12; this is not merely a preregistration or abstract. Input URL e9j6y differs from the report project qgm2c; the input reference itself names qgm2c, which matches the report. The broader Parsons et al. listing and listing date are not independently confirmed. No PDF was supplied. This row has no replication study identifier, claim ID, outcome description or locator. Five distinct claims are reported. Input order, original metric labels and the original-only p. 8 locator cannot securely identify a replication claim. Row-specific correspondence is unresolved. Candidate discrepancies: mov8w7 narrative prints p = 0.001, while Table R.1 marks -0.08*** and defines *** as p < .001. md71wp narrative prints p = 0.072 and not replicated, while Table R.2 marks -0.07* and defines * as p < .05; its narrative result says 2-year college but inferential criteria and table identify 4-year college. mrdnoj methods identify Cox regression, while Table R.3 labels logistic regression and explicitly defines OR as odds ratio. Keep these printed identities and conflicts; no conversion or reconciliation. ser_method is not a printed effect metric.
